intro.title: auto-fit and minmax()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a responsive grid layout that automatically adjusts the number of columns based on the available screen width. You will learn to use the CSS Grid properties auto-fit and minmax() to create flexible, fluid grids without media queries. The core concept involves defining a grid with columns that have a minimum size but can expand to fill the space, with auto-fit handling the column count dynamically. You'll work with CSS Grid syntax, specifically the repeat() function combined with these properties. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you create layouts that look great on any device.
intro.usecase: The auto-fit and minmax() functions are essential for creating responsive grid layouts that adapt to different screen sizes. You'll use this pattern in product dashboards where card-based content needs to rearrange itself automatically as users resize their browser windows. E-commerce sites employ these functions to display product grids that maintain minimum card widths while filling available space efficiently. News websites use auto-fit with minmax() to create flexible article layouts that work seamlessly on mobile, tablet, and desktop devices without media query clutter.
